summary: Harivallabh Bhayani (1917–2001) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Samaldas Arts College (~1935–1939) and Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan (~1945–1951), later serving as Director of the L.D. Institute of Indology.

Harjot Oberoi is a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the Australian National University (~1983–1987) and held a post at the University of British Columbia around 1987.

Harold Conklin (1926–2016) worked in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley (~1947–1950) and Yale University (~1949–1955), and held an academic post at Columbia University (~1954–1962).

Harold G. Coward (born 1936) is an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar. He was a Professor at the University of Calgary (~1974–1992) and later held a post at the University of Victoria (~1992–2004).

Harold Hargreaves (1876–1951) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Officiating Director General of Archæology in India at the Archaeological Survey of India in 1914 and from 1928 to 1931.

Harold Scheub (1931–2019) studied at the University of Michigan (~1954–1960) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1965–1969). He held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from around 1970 to 2013.
Harold Stewart (1916–1995) was a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed his education at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music and the University of Sydney.

Harold Walter Bailey (1899–1996) was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, Indological, and linguistic studies. He studied at the University of Western Australia (~1921–1927) and served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Cambridge (1938–1967).
Hartmut Buescher works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Chandrabhal Tripathi and held posts at the University of Copenhagen and the Royal Danish Library.
Hartmut Scharfe (1932–2020) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He completed his doctoral studies under Paul Thieme and held a position at the University of California, Los Angeles.

Hartmut-Ortwin Feistel worked in Indology. He served as head at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 1989) and held a post in the Oriental Department at the Berlin State Library (attested 1992–1994).

Haruhiko Masaki (born 1938) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his master's degree at the University of Tokyo and held a professorship at Nagasaki University (attested 1988).
Haruka Yanagisawa (1944–2015) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1992–2007) and Chiba University (attested 2005).

Harumi Hirano Ziegler is a scholar of Buddhist studies. She earned her MA (completed 1994) and PhD (completed 2001) from the University of California, Los Angeles, studying under doctoral supervisor Robert E. Buswell Jr.

Harunaga Isaacson (born 1965), an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar, studied at Groningen and Leiden. He held posts at Groningen, Oxford, and Pennsylvania, and became Professor at the University of Hamburg in 2006.

Harushige Kōzu (1908–1973) was a linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Oxford (~1937–1939). He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo (~1942–1969) and Musashi University (~1969–1973).

Harvey B. Aronson works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Supervised for his doctorate by Richard Hugh Robinson, he held a professorship at the University of Virginia (attested 1988) and served as Co-director of the Dawn Mountain Center for Tibetan Buddhism (attested 2001).
Haya Akegarasu (1877–1954) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He studied at Otani University from around 1899 to 1902 and at the Tokyo School of Foreign Languages.

Heather Stoddard is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1966–1970) with D. C. Lau, and was also supervised by Nicole Vandier-Nicolas (~1977–1982) and taught by Samten Gyaltsen Karmay.
Hegoda Khemananda is a Buddhist studies scholar. In 1993, he was attested as Vice Principal at Vidyodaya Pirivena and as Director at Dharma Paryeshanalaya.
